title: Why the First Amendment’s forgotten right of assembly matters more than ever
summary_en: WashU’s John Inazu argues that the ability to gather with others is essential to a healthy democracy — particularly at a time of deep social and political division. He was among the faculty presenting as part of the John C. Danforth Center on Religion and Politics course “1776: Then and Now.”
title_cn: Why the First Amendment’s forgotten right of assembly matters more than ever

title: Ebola and public health preparedness during the World Cup
summary_en: As millions travel for the World Cup, Jennifer Layden of WashU Bursky Public Health explains how officials track outbreaks, assess risk and prepare for emerging infectious disease threats.
title_cn: Ebola and public health preparedness during the World Cup

title: Socioeconomic factors linked to lasting imprint in kids’ brains
summary_en: A study led by WashU Medicine researchers shows that a family’s financial situation and the resources and opportunities in a child’s neighborhood had the strongest connection to brain development, accounting for 16% of the variability in measures of children’s brain function — far more than IQ, parenting style, health history or any other factor.
title_cn: Socioeconomic factors linked to lasting imprint in kids’ brains

title: Glauber installed as inaugural Miriam Barr Librarian for Jewish and Near Eastern Studies
summary_en: A scholar of modern Jewish history specializing in East European Jewry and its diaspora communities, Samuel Glauber’s work has appeared in numerous journals.
title_cn: Glauber installed as inaugural Miriam Barr Librarian for Jewish and Near Eastern Studies

title: New research reveals how brains update their predictions
summary_en: Researchers in Bruce Carlson’s lab at WashU study electric fish to understand the basics of brain sensory processing and prediction.
title_cn: New research reveals how brains update their predictions

title: Provost announces leadership transitions
summary_en: Several faculty members have been appointed to new leadership positions in the Office of the Provost at WashU, effective by July 1, Provost Mark West announced.

title: Karch named inaugural Barbara Burton and Reuben M. Morriss III Professor
summary_en: Celeste Karch was recognized for pioneering Alzheimer’s research, advancing stem cell, genomic and collaborative neurodegeneration studies.
title_cn: Karch named inaugural Barbara Burton and Reuben M. Morriss III Professor

title: WashU partners with St. Louis to expand CLEAN STL tornado recovery project
summary_en: Washington University in St. Louis is formally partnering with St. Louis to expand environmental monitoring and public health research in city neighborhoods affected by the devastating May 16, 2025, tornado.
title_cn: WashU partners with St. Louis to expand CLEAN STL tornado recovery project

title: WashU Athletics wins Learfield Directors’ Cup
summary_en: For the first time in program history, the WashU Bears have won the Learfield Directors’ Cup, presented by the National Association of Collegiate Directors of Athletics, the organization announced June 9. The Directors’ Cup is widely considered the ultimate measurement of overall athletic program success in collegiate sports.
title_cn: WashU Athletics wins Learfield Directors’ Cup

title: Targeting tumor metabolism to fight cancer
summary_en: Cancer cells are ravenous eaters. WashU’s Gary Patti is trying to turn their hunger against them.
title_cn: Targeting tumor metabolism to fight cancer
